per_task.prompt: Design a multi-tenant API rate limiter that must be FAIR across tenants with wildly different traffic volumes (some 10 req/s, some 10k req/s), degrade gracefully when the shared Redis backend is unavailable, and avoid BOTH per-tenant starvation AND global thundering-herd on limit reset. Specify: the data structures, the exact algorithm for allow/deny, the fairness mechanism, the Redis-outage failure semantics, and the THREE subtlest correctness pitfalls someone implementing this would most likely get wrong (with why). Be concrete and rigorous.

arms.answer:
# Multi-Tenant Fair Rate Limiter — Design

## 1. Core algorithmic choice (and why it kills the thundering herd at the root)

Use **GCRA (Generic Cell Rate Algorithm)** per enforcement point, **not** fixed-window counters. GCRA is a continuous-refill formulation of a token/leaky bucket that stores a **single scalar per limiter — the TAT (Theoretical Arrival Time)** — and has **no reset instant**. Fixed windows (`INCR key:minute; EXPIRE`) create a synchronized boundary at `:00` where every tenant's counter zeroes simultaneously → global burst. GCRA has no boundary to synchronize on, so the primary thundering-herd source is eliminated by construction. The secondary source (synchronized client *retries*) is handled in §5, pitfall #3.

GCRA at rate `R` with burst `B`:
- Emission interval `T = 1/R`; burst tolerance `τ = (B−1)·T`.
- State: `TAT` (a timestamp).
- Decision at time `t`:
  - `allow_at = TAT − τ`
  - if `t < allow_at` → **DENY**, `retry_after = allow_at − t`
  - else → `TAT' = max(TAT, t) + cost·T`; persist; **ALLOW**
- The check is **pure** until the ALLOW commit — critical for composing two tiers (pitfall #2).

## 2. Fairness model — two tiers: guaranteed floor + weighted shared spare

Wildly asymmetric tenants (10 req/s vs 10k req/s) cannot be made fair by a single shared counter (the 10k tenant wins every race) nor by pure per-tenant isolation (wastes idle capacity and isn't work-conserving). Use **committed floor + max-min-fair spare**:

Provisioning (admission control, done once): each tenant `i` has committed rate `r_i`, committed burst `B_i`, and weight `w_i`. Global backend capacity `G`. Enforce `Σ r_i ≤ G` at provisioning time; **spare rate `P = G − Σr_i`** is the redistributable pool.

**Tier 1 — Committed floor (isolation / anti-starvation guarantee).**
A per-tenant GCRA at rate `r_i`, burst `B_i`. This capacity is *always* available to tenant `i` regardless of what any other tenant does. This is the formal starvation-freedom guarantee: no traffic pattern by others can drive `i` below `r_i`.

**Tier 2 — Shared spare (work-conserving fairness).**
When a request exceeds Tier 1, it may *borrow* from spare `P`. Borrowing must pass **both** limiters atomically:
- **(a) Per-tenant fair-share limiter** — GCRA at rate `share_i = (w_i / W) · P`, where `W = Σ w_j` over tenants *currently demanding spare*. This prevents the 10k tenant from monopolizing `P`.
- **(b) Global spare bucket** — one token bucket at rate `P`, burst `P·window`. This hard-caps *total* spare draw so per-share rounding/skew can never overshoot `G`.

Request ALLOWs on spare **iff (a) AND (b) both allow**; then consume both. Idle tenants drop out of `W` (see below), so their share redistributes to the busy ones → work-conserving, weighted **max-min fairness** (approximate; the honest limitation is below).

## 3. Data structures

Redis (authoritative), per tenant `i`:
| Key | Type | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `rl:{i}:c` | string | Tier-1 committed TAT (µs). TTL = `⌈τ_c + T_c⌉` (drain time). |
| `rl:{i}:s` | string | Tier-2 per-tenant fair-share TAT. TTL = share drain time. |
| `rl:global` | hash | `{tokens, ts}` — global spare bucket. No TTL. |
| `rl:demand` | zset | member=tenant, score=last-borrow-attempt ts. Members within `Δ` (e.g. 1 s) = "currently demanding spare"; `W` = sum of their weights. TTL-pruned by score. |
| `rl:nodes` | zset | node heartbeats, score=ts → live node count `N` for fallback sizing. |

Config (`r_i, B_i, w_i`) lives in a versioned config store, cached at each node with a short TTL and a version epoch (pitfall discussion).

Per node (in-memory, for degraded mode): a mirror `LocalGCRA` per tenant, a Redis **circuit breaker**, and last-known `N`.

`W` is not summed per request (O(active) is too costly at 10k req/s): maintain a running weighted-demand aggregate refreshed every ~100 ms by a background sweep of `rl:demand`, cached at nodes.

## 4. Exact allow/deny algorithm (single atomic Lua script — one round trip)

The **entire two-tier decision is one `EVALSHA`** so it is atomic under Redis's single-threaded execution. Time comes from **`redis.call('TIME')` inside the script**, never from the client (pitfall #1).

```
-- KEYS = rl:{i}:c, rl:{i}:s, rl:global, rl:demand
-- ARGV = r_i,B_i, w_i, W, P, cost, ttl_c, ttl_s, demand_win
local t = now_micros_from(redis.call('TIME'))
local Tc, tau_c = 1/r_i, (B_i-1)/r_i

-- TIER 1: committed (pure check first)
local tat = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])) or t
if t >= tat - tau_c then
    redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], math.max(tat,t) + cost*Tc, 'PX', ttl_c)
    return {'ALLOW','committed'}
end

-- TIER 2: borrow. Mark demand FIRST so W reflects reality.
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[4], t, tenant)
local share = (w_i / W) * P
local Ts, tau_s = 1/share, (share_burst-1)/share

-- (a) per-tenant fair share (pure check)
local stat = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[2])) or t
if t < stat - tau_s then
    return {'DENY','share', retry_after=(stat - tau_s - t)}   -- NO state mutated
end
-- (b) global spare bucket (pure check)
local g = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[3], 'tokens','ts')
local tok = math.min(P*win, (tonumber(g[1]) or P*win) + (t-(tonumber(g[2]) or t))*P)
if tok < cost then
    return {'DENY','global', retry_after=(cost-tok)/P}         -- NO state mutated
end
-- COMMIT: both passed → charge BOTH, never one without the other
redis.call('SET', KEYS[2], math.max(stat,t) + cost*Ts, 'PX', ttl_s)
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[3], 'tokens', tok - cost, 'ts', t)
return {'ALLOW','spare'}
```

Key invariants: (1) Tier-1 TAT is mutated **only** on committed-ALLOW; (2) spare state is mutated **only** when both (a) and (b) pass; (3) a DENY never charges anything. This is what makes composition correct.

## 5. Redis-outage failure semantics

Wrap every `EVALSHA` in a **circuit breaker** with a tight budget (timeout ~5–10 ms; trip on N consecutive timeouts/errors). Breaker states drive the policy:

**Closed (healthy):** authoritative path above.

**Open (Redis down):** fall back to **per-node local GCRA**, sized to a bounded per-node share so the fleet can't collectively overshoot without coordination:
- Local committed cap `= r_i / N_eff`, where `N_eff = max(last_known_N, N_min)` (last node count from `rl:nodes`, floored). Multiply by a safety factor `< 1` because load balancers rarely spread a tenant's traffic evenly, so per-node caps summed can exceed `G` if you assume perfect balance.
- Local spare is **disabled by default** in degraded mode (spare requires global coordination that Redis provided; without it you cannot bound total draw). Committed floors still hold → tenants keep their guarantees; only opportunistic burst is lost.
- Policy is **per-route**: default = *fail-degraded* (enforce local caps — not fail-open, not fail-closed) so a single node can't unboundedly flood; abuse-sensitive routes (auth, payment) = *fail-closed*; pure-availability routes may *fail-open*. Never a blanket global choice.

**Half-open (recovery):** probes must be **jittered per node** (decorrelated) or all nodes reconnect together and stampede Redis. On recovery, **do not trust stale TAT blindly**: if `now − TAT ≫ τ`, a tenant that was idle would be handed a full instantaneous burst → a recovery thundering herd. Reconcile by `TAT ← max(TAT_redis, TAT_local, now − τ)` (clamp to "now minus one burst") and best-effort merge local consumption back. Ramp spare back gradually.

## 6. The three subtlest pitfalls (highest-probability real bugs)

**Pitfall 1 — Passing the client's wall clock into the GCRA math instead of using Redis's own clock.**
GCRA arithmetic is timestamp subtraction on a *shared* TAT. If each app node sends its own `now` into the script, **clock skew corrupts shared state**: a node whose NTP runs fast writes `TAT` into the future and denies everyone else; a slow node undercounts and lets the tenant overspend. It passes every single-node test and only manifests as unfair denials under fleet skew. Fix: compute time with `redis.call('TIME')` inside the (atomic) script — one authoritative clock. The *second-order* trap: `TIME` is non-deterministic, so on Redis versions using command-replication a script calling `TIME` would replicate differently to replicas/AOF and diverge — you must rely on **effects-based replication** (default in Redis ≥5) or you'll get replica drift. Also guard against wall-clock **backward steps** (NTP correction): a backward jump makes `now < TAT − τ` for everyone → mass false-DENY. Clamp `now = max(now, TAT − τ_max)` or prefer a monotonic source where available.

**Pitfall 2 — Partial charging when composing the two tiers (charging a tier for a request you then deny).**
The naive implementation runs Tier-1 as one operation, sees DENY, then runs Tier-2 as a *separate* operation. If the Tier-1 step **mutates** TAT during its "check" (many hand-rolled buckets do a read-modify-write in the check), you've now consumed a committed token for a request that Tier-2 rejects. That capacity leaks permanently, and under sustained load the tenant is charged for requests it never got served → **slow starvation of the exact tenant fairness was meant to protect**. Even correct per-tier logic breaks if the two tiers aren't in one atomic script: concurrent requests double-spend the global spare bucket via read-modify-write races. Fix: single Lua script; every tier's check is **pure**; **state is written only on the final ALLOW**, and spare requires *both* (a) and (b) to pass before *either* is charged (no partial commit). This is why GCRA's "check is pure until commit" property was chosen over an INCR-first scheme.

**Pitfall 3 — Fixing the server-side reset herd but re-creating it client-side via synchronized `Retry-After`.**
GCRA removes the server reset boundary, so implementers think the herd is solved. But if every denied caller is told the *same* `retry_after` (the exact `allow_at`, or worse rounded up to the next whole second / next `X-RateLimit-Reset` wall-clock boundary), **all rejected clients retry at the same instant** and re-collide — a self-inflicted stampede that the server can't see in its own logic. It's subtle because the limiter is provably correct; the herd lives in the advertised timing. Fixes, all needed: (a) return `retry_after` with **per-request decorrelated jitter** — a random value in `[allow_at, allow_at + jitter]`; (b) never align any window/reset you expose to a shared wall-clock boundary — **phase-shift per tenant by `hash(tenant_id)`** so tenants don't reset in lockstep; (c) require clients to honor `Retry-After` with exponential + jittered backoff, and have the server escalate penalties on ignore. The honorable-mention cousin: setting the **TTL on idle buckets too short** (to reclaim memory) drops TAT, so a returning idle tenant gets a free full burst — TTL must be exactly the drain time `⌈τ + T⌉`, long enough that no reclaim happens while the bucket is non-empty, short enough to eventually evict truly-idle tenants.

## Honest limitations
- The spare fairness is **approximate max-min**: `W` is sampled every ~100 ms, so during rapid churn in the demanding set a tenant can transiently get slightly more/less than its weighted share. The global spare bucket (b) still hard-bounds total draw, so this is a fairness-jitter issue, not a capacity-safety one.
- Degraded mode trades exactness for availability: with `N` estimated and imperfect LB balancing, total committed throughput during an outage can overshoot `G` by the safety-factor margin. That is an explicit, bounded, documented tradeoff — not silent.
- `Σ r_i ≤ G` is an admission-control obligation at provisioning; if you oversell committed rates, the starvation-freedom guarantee no longer holds because the floors themselves contend.

# Multi-Tenant Fair Rate Limiter — Design

## 0. Architecture in one paragraph

N stateless gateway nodes enforce limits by calling a single atomic Lua script against a shared Redis (Cluster). The admission algorithm is **GCRA (Generic Cell Rate Algorithm)** per tenant — one float of state, continuous refill, so there is *no window boundary and therefore no reset instant to herd on*. Cross-tenant fairness is **not** done in the hot path: a low-frequency **water-filling controller** computes weighted max-min fair ceilings from *offered* demand and pushes them to nodes; the hot path enforces `min(configured_rate, fair_ceiling)` with a single-key atomic script. On Redis outage, each node degrades to a local monotonic-clock GCRA at `guaranteed_rate / N`, which keeps the aggregate below cluster capacity and preserves every tenant's floor (fail-degraded, neither fail-open nor fail-closed).

---

## 1. Data structures

**Redis (all tenant keys use hash-tag `{T}` so they share a cluster slot):**

| Key | Type | Contents | TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rl:{T}:tat` | string (float, µs) | GCRA Theoretical Arrival Time | `≥ tat − now` (see Pitfall 3c) |
| `rl:{T}:demand` | hash | `slot:<epoch-sec> → offered cost` (2–3 rolling 1s slots) | 3 s |
| `rl:{T}:cfg` | hash | `rate r_T, burst b_T, weight w_T, guarantee g_T, max_ceiling` | none |
| `rl:alloc` | hash | tenant → effective ceiling `c_T` (+ version) | none (controller-owned) |
| `rl:node:<id>` | string | heartbeat | 3 s |
| `rl:tenants` | set | tenant registry for controller SCAN-free iteration | none |

**Per gateway node (in memory):**

- Read-through caches of `cfg` and `rl:alloc` (TTL ~1 s + pub/sub invalidation, refresh jittered ±20%).
- **Shadow local GCRA state per tenant** (`tat_local` on the **monotonic** clock), maintained continuously even while Redis is healthy, so failover starts warm.
- Circuit breaker per Redis shard (Cluster: per slot-range, so a partial outage only degrades tenants on dead slots).
- Cached live-node count `N_live` from heartbeat keys, **frozen at last-known value when the breaker opens**.

State cost: O(1) per tenant (~120 bytes in Redis). Hot path: exactly 1 `EVALSHA` per request.

---

## 2. Exact allow/deny algorithm

### 2.1 Node-side (per request, cost `c ≥ 1`)

```
cfg  = cache.cfg(T)                       # miss → Redis; miss during outage → conservative default (1 rps)
ceil = cache.alloc(T) or cfg.rate         # fairness ceiling, may be stale ≤ 1s
r    = min(cfg.rate, ceil);  Tint = 1e6 / r  (µs/token);  b = cfg.burst
if c > b: return 400 "cost exceeds burst"          # NOT 429 — no Retry-After can ever satisfy it
if breaker.closed:
    res = EVALSHA(gcra, keys=[rl:{T}:tat, rl:{T}:demand], argv=[Tint, b, c, ...])
    on error/timeout(5ms): breaker.record_fail(); goto LOCAL
    also feed the decision into the shadow local bucket (keep it warm)
    return res
LOCAL:  # outage mode, §4
    r_local = cfg.g_T / N_frozen;  local monotonic-clock GCRA at (r_local, b·g_T/(r·N_frozen))
```

### 2.2 Redis Lua (atomic; effects-replication)

```lua
-- KEYS[1]=rl:{T}:tat  KEYS[2]=rl:{T}:demand
-- ARGV[1]=Tint(µs/token) ARGV[2]=burst b ARGV[3]=cost c
redis.replicate_commands()                    -- required before TIME on old Redis; default ≥5
local t   = redis.call('TIME')
local now = t[1]*1000000 + t[2]               -- single time authority: Redis, not the caller
local Ti  = tonumber(ARGV[1]); local b = tonumber(ARGV[2]); local c = tonumber(ARGV[3])

-- (A) demand accounting: OFFERED load, incremented BEFORE the decision (Pitfall 1)
local slot = math.floor(now/1000000)
redis.call('HINCRBY', KEYS[2], slot, c);  redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[2], 3000)

local tat = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])) or now
if tat < now then tat = now end               -- idle credit accrues, capped by burst below
local new_tat = tat + c*Ti
if new_tat - now <= b*Ti then                 -- debt after admission fits within burst
    local ttl = math.ceil((new_tat - now)/1000) + 60000   -- covers full TAT horizon (Pitfall 3c)
    redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], new_tat, 'PX', ttl)
    return {1, math.floor((b*Ti - (new_tat - now))/Ti), 0}      -- allow, remaining, 0
else
    local retry = (tat + c*Ti - b*Ti) - now   -- computed from UNMODIFIED tat (Pitfall 2a)
    return {0, 0, retry}                      -- deny; state untouched
end
```

Properties: exactly `b` requests admitted from cold in one instant; steady-state rate exactly `r`; **refill is continuous**, so quota "reset" as a synchronized event does not exist — the classic top-of-minute thundering herd is eliminated by construction, not by jitter band-aids.

Node adds `Retry-After = ceil((retry + U(0, c·Ti))/1e6)` — jittered, see Pitfall 2b — plus `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset`.

---

## 3. Fairness mechanism (weighted max-min, no starvation)

Every tenant has a **guarantee** `g_T > 0` with `Σ g_T ≤ 0.7·C` (C = protected cluster capacity) and a weight `w_T`. Every Δ = 500 ms, a controller (leader via `SET NX PX` lease with fencing version; computation is deterministic so a brief dual-leader episode is last-writer-wins-safe):

1. Reads `rl:{T}:demand` for tenants in `rl:tenants`, computes EWMA offered demand `d_T` (α ≈ 0.3).
2. Excess demand `e_T = max(0, d_T − g_T)`; pool `P = C − Σ g_T`.
3. **Water-filling**: find λ s.t. `Σ min(e_T, w_T·λ) = P`; ceiling `c_T = min(cfg.max_ceiling, g_T + min(e_T, w_T·λ))`.
4. **Slew-rate limit**: `c_T` may at most double per interval on the way up (Pitfall 2b, macro-herd damping); drops apply immediately.
5. `HSET rl:alloc` + `PUBLISH rl:invalidate`.

Why this is fair and starvation-free:
- A 10 req/s tenant's demand sits below the water level → it *always* receives its full demand; the 10k req/s tenant absorbs all of the throttling. That is exactly max-min fairness.
- Under total overload every tenant still holds `g_T > 0` — a hard floor independent of anyone else's behavior.
- Max-min is demand-exaggeration-resistant: reporting demand above the water level does not raise your allocation, so a flooding tenant cannot distort the allocation of others.
- Bounded overshoot: enforcement of `c_T` lags demand by ≤ Δ + cache TTL, so aggregate can exceed C by at most `Σ(ceiling raises) × ~1.5 s`. This is why C must be set with 10–20% headroom below true capacity — the design deliberately trades hot-path cross-key atomicity (impossible across Cluster slots anyway) for an asynchronous, *boundedly*-stale global constraint.

At the 10k req/s end, one EVALSHA per request is ~10k ops/s per hot tenant — fine for Redis (>100k ops/s/shard). If Redis CPU or RTT becomes the limit, add **token leasing** (a node leases batches of `n = max(1, r·RTT·2)` admissions per tenant, lease TTL ~200 ms): amortizes round trips at the price of ≤ `N·n` admission slack per tenant, which must be counted inside the burst budget — and unused leases must simply expire, never be "returned" (the return path races with re-lease and double-credits).

---

## 4. Redis-outage failure semantics (fail-degraded)

- **Detection**: 5 ms hard timeout on EVALSHA; breaker opens on 10 consecutive failures or >50% errors over 2 s. A *slow* Redis is treated as a *down* Redis — the limiter may never become the availability bottleneck.
- **While open**: each node enforces local GCRA per tenant at `g_T / N_frozen` (`N_frozen` = last healthy heartbeat count; a node that boots mid-outage assumes configured max fleet size — conservative). Worst-case aggregate admitted = `Σ g_T ≤ 0.7·C` even if all nodes are partitioned from Redis simultaneously → the backend is protected. Every tenant keeps its floor → no starvation during the outage. Explicit, documented trade-off: big tenants lose burst/borrowed headroom during outages; small tenants (demand < guarantee) feel nothing.
- **Unknown tenant during outage** (cfg cache miss): fail-closed to a 1 req/s default bucket. Untrusted growth doesn't get free rein exactly when observability is degraded.
- **Recovery**: half-open with *one* probe per node per 500 ms (request coalescing — never one probe per user request), then **jittered rejoin** over U(0, 5 s) per node so a cold/recovering Redis is not hit by N nodes × full traffic at the same millisecond (thundering herd *on recovery* is as real as on reset). Local state is discarded, **never merged back**: GCRA's `max(tat, now)` makes the authoritative state self-forgiving — replaying outage-time admissions into Redis would double-count and cause a deny storm.
- **Partial outage** (some Cluster slots down): per-slot breakers; only tenants hashed there degrade.

---

## 5. The three subtlest pitfalls

**Pitfall 1 — Feeding the fairness controller *admitted* load instead of *offered* load (starvation lock-in).**
If `d_T` is measured from allowed requests, a throttled tenant's measured demand equals its current ceiling. Water-filling then concludes "demand satisfied" and never raises that ceiling, while capacity freed elsewhere flows to tenants that happen to hold high ceilings. The system freezes into whatever allocation existed at the first overload — a hysteresis trap that looks like correct behavior in every unit test (each component is "working") and only appears as slow, permanent unfairness in production. That is why the `HINCRBY` in the script executes **before** the allow/deny branch, on the deny path too. Related second-order trap: EWMA time constant vs. Δ — too slow and reallocation oscillates (capacity released a full second after a burst ends gets granted to a tenant that no longer wants it); damp with the ×2-per-interval slew limit.

**Pitfall 2 — Deny-path TAT semantics: both possible choices are wrong in one direction each, and you must know which wrongness you picked.**
(a) If deny *advances* TAT ("count denied traffic against the bucket"), a tenant offering 3× its rate accumulates unbounded future debt while receiving 0% throughput; when it slows back to a compliant rate it stays locked out (TAT is minutes in the future), and anyone who merely *knows* a tenant's API key can DoS it for free with rejected requests. So deny must leave state untouched — as in the script. (b) But *because* deny leaves state untouched, every request denied in the same instant receives the **identical** `retry` value → they all come back in the same millisecond, get denied together, and recohere forever: a self-sustaining per-tenant micro-herd that continuous refill does *not* fix. The fix is deliberate desynchronization: server-side jitter `U(0, c·Ti)` on Retry-After, plus the controller's slew-limited, phase-jittered ceiling raises so that after a global squeeze all tenants don't regain headroom in the same control tick (the macro version of the same herd).

**Pitfall 3 — Time authority, replication, and debt-forgiving TTLs (three coupled clock bugs).**
(a) Passing gateway wall-clock time into the script: with N nodes and skew s, a fast-clock node silently grants extra burst (`s/Ti` tokens) and a slow one emits negative Retry-After; use `redis.call('TIME')` — one clock for one datum. (b) Doing so makes the script non-deterministic, which is only safe under **effects replication** (`redis.replicate_commands()`; default on Redis ≥ 5) — under verbatim script replication the replica re-executes with a *different* `now` and the TAT diverges. Also accept that failover to an async replica loses the last moments of TAT advancement: burst amplification ≈ `rate × replication_lag`, which is another reason C carries headroom — don't pretend exactly-once. (c) TTL: setting the key TTL to "the window" (e.g., 1 s) instead of `≥ tat − now` means a tenant that overdrafts with a high-cost request and then goes idle for TTL gets its entire debt expired — a pause-to-reset exploit that inverts the limiter for exactly the bursty clients it exists to police. TTL must cover the full TAT horizon (the script computes it per write). And in the local fallback path, use the **monotonic** clock: an NTP step during a Redis outage (when you have no authority to cross-check) otherwise spuriously refills or freezes every local bucket at once.

*Honorable mentions (excluded from the top three because they're better-known):* GET-then-SET instead of one Lua script (over-admission ∝ concurrency); trying to check tenant-key + global-pool atomically across Cluster slots (impossible — the async-ceiling architecture exists precisely to avoid needing it); refunding cost on downstream failure (the refund races with concurrent admissions and is gameable — don't, or cap it); `cost > burst` returning 429 with an unsatisfiable Retry-After instead of 400.

# MULTI-TENANT RATE LIMITER — DESIGN SPECIFICATION

## 0. Fairness semantics (fixed first — everything depends on it)
HYBRID: per-tenant contracted FLOOR (primary, exact) + optional weighted share of GLOBAL SPARE (secondary, best-effort).
- Floor/isolation invariant (no starvation): each tenant i is admitted up to contracted rate r_i (burst b_i) using its OWN private state, independent of all others. A 10k-req/s tenant physically cannot advance a 10-req/s tenant's state. This is exact and load-bearing.
- No-monopoly: above its floor a tenant borrows from a global spare pool with a per-tenant cap. HONEST SCOPE: this layer is approximate, not a clean global invariant (see §3). Treat the floor as the contract, the pool as opportunistic.
Why floor+spare, not pure global max-min: a contractual guarantee must not shrink as the active set grows; pure max-min starves the low-volume tenant below contract when many tenants are active. A private floor decouples the contract from contention; only surplus is contended.

## 1. Data structures
REDIS (authoritative):
- rl:t:{tid} -> single value TAT (GCRA Theoretical Arrival Time, ms). Only mutable per-tenant floor state, O(1). PEXPIRE >= tau_i+T_i refreshed on EVERY access (Pitfall 2).
- rl:cfg:{tid} -> HASH {rate,burst,weight}, node-cached ~1s. T_i=1000/r_i ms; tau_i=(b_i-1)*T_i (burst of exactly b_i).
- rl:pool -> global spare bucket {tokens,last_ms}, refill = C - Sum(r_i) (spare AFTER floors, NOT C). Require Sum(r_i) <= C.
- rl:lease:{tid}:{leaseId} -> {granted,ts}, short TTL so a crashed node's lease is reclaimed by expiry, not by trusting the node.
- rlbill:{tid}:{period} -> exact billing counter, decoupled, never gates admission.
PER NODE (non-authoritative): lease cache (high-volume only, local decrement 0-RTT); per-tenant fallback GCRA (breaker-open only); circuit-breaker FSM; optional short-TTL negative cache. NEVER cache ALLOW.

## 2. Allow/deny algorithm (single atomic Lua script)
Redis is single-threaded, so the script's read-compare-conditional-write is indivisible: two nodes can never both see 'under limit' and double-spend the SAME key. `now` is read INSIDE the script via redis.call('TIME') (one authoritative clock) with redis.replicate_commands() so EFFECTS, not the non-deterministic script, replicate.

  redis.replicate_commands()
  local t=redis.call('TIME'); local now=t[1]*1000+math.floor(t[2]/1000)
  local T,tau,cost=tonumber(ARGV[1]),tonumber(ARGV[2]),tonumber(ARGV[3])
  local tat=tonumber(redis.call('GET',KEYS[1])) or now
  local allow_at=tat-tau
  if now<allow_at then return {0, allow_at-now} end        -- DENY, retry_after_ms
  local new_tat=math.max(tat,now)+cost*T
  redis.call('SET',KEYS[1],new_tat,'PX',math.ceil(tau)+T+1000)  -- TTL on EVERY write
  return {1,0}                                              -- ALLOW

Path: (1) local lease remaining>0 -> decrement, ALLOW (0 RTT); else (2) low-volume: script per request; (3) high-volume: lease-acquire variant advances TAT by K*T, serves K locally; (4) if floor denies and spare enabled, attempt pool (§3).
retry_after MUST be jittered: retry_after*(1+rand*j). Deny does not advance TAT, so every request in a burst otherwise reads identical TAT -> identical retry -> clients retry in lockstep = a client-side herd that survives continuous accounting.
Root fix for reset-herd: GCRA capacity is a CONTINUOUS function of time — no instant when a counter snaps to zero, so no synchronized reset boundary, unlike fixed/sliding windows resetting at t mod W==0 for all tenants at once. If exact billing windows are mandated, keep them in rlbill only, evaluated lazily, anchored per tenant at phase=hash(tid) mod W to desynchronize.

## 3. Fairness mechanism — and its honest limits
- No-starvation (exact): private key rl:t:{tid}, zero cross-tenant coupling. Floor decided FIRST, never touches the pool.
- No-monopoly (best-effort): above floor, borrow from rl:pool refilling at C-Sum(r_i), with per-tenant weighted borrow cap.
TWO corrections the naive version gets wrong:
1. Pool sized to C-Sum(r_i), NOT C. A C-sized pool plus floor traffic (up to Sum(r_i)) accounted nowhere in the pool reaches C+Sum(r_i).
2. 'total<=C' is a RATE bound, not instantaneous. Floors carry burst tau_i and the pool its own depth, so an instantaneous multi-tenant burst can reach Sum(b_i)+pool_depth. Claim a long-run rate ceiling plus a bounded, sized aggregate burst — not a hard instantaneous C.
STRUCTURAL LIMITATION (the honest core caveat): a per-tenant key and a shared pool key are DIFFERENT keys; Redis Lua is atomic only within one shard/slot.
- Single instance / all keys hash-tagged to one slot: floor+pool script is truly atomic, but the pool + hot-tenant keys become a single-slot hotspot that hurts the 10k tenant.
- Redis Cluster: cannot atomically touch a per-tenant key on slot A and the pool on slot B (CROSSSLOT). Either shard the pool (-> approximate global cap) or hash-tag everything to one slot (-> hotspot). No free lunch: exact global fairness across a cluster costs either the cap's exactness or the sharding the 10k tenant needs. This design treats the FLOOR as exact and the POOL as approximate, and says so.
- Work-conservation caveat: a fixed borrow cap can deny a single active tenant above its floor while capacity sits idle. If work-conservation matters more, the cap must be dynamic (raised when few tenants active) — reintroducing aggregator cost.
Weighted borrow shares are recomputed OFF the fast path by a ~1s water-filling max-min aggregator; the fast path stays O(1) GCRA.

## 4. Redis-outage semantics (+ recovery)
Detection: per-call timeout (5-20ms) + circuit breaker; k consecutive failures -> OPEN; periodic half-open probe.
Degraded (bounded local fallback, per-tenant-class, NOT a global binary):
- Each node runs local GCRA at r_i/N_est (continuous — no local reset herd). Freeze the spare pool (serve floors only).
- Policy split: hard-quota/billing tenants -> fail-CLOSED to floor-only (brief 429 beats un-billable traffic); availability-critical -> fail-OPEN but CAPPED at a bounded multiple of r_i/N_est. NEVER unbounded fail-open (amplifies a blip into a backend outage).
- N_est = max(N_min_configured, last_known_healthy), biased HIGH: over-estimating N under-admits (safe); under-estimating over-admits (dangerous). True live count is unobservable during a partition without a coordinator.
- Honest limit: r_i/N_est per node only approximates r_i under EVEN spread. A low-volume tenant concentrated on few nodes can be throttled BELOW contract, and each node grants a full tau_i burst so worst-case aggregate burst is N_est x. Fallback is graceful-degradation, not exact. Local admissions logged for reconciliation. Local fallback uses the node MONOTONIC clock (oracle gone), kept node-local so skew cannot corrupt shared state.
Recovery (avoid a SECOND herd):
- Reconnect de-herd: probe after t0+Uniform(0,2s); close breaker only on success.
- No free burst: first post-outage write seeds TAT=max(stored_TAT,now), NOT now-tau (that would mint a full fresh tolerance burst for every tenant at once = a reset herd through recovery).
- Clamp lazy refill: credit min(elapsed, one_bucket), set last_ms=now (else huge elapsed saturates the pool in one step).
- Admission is FORGIVEN, billing reconciled separately. Do NOT back-charge outage admissions to the admission TAT — advancing TAT pushes allow_at into the future and denies in-floor requests until the debt clears, CREATING the starvation the floor prevents. Repay quota debt only in the decoupled billing meter.

## 5. THE THREE SUBTLEST PITFALLS (mechanistic why)
PITFALL 1 — Passing the node wall clock as ARGV instead of reading Redis TIME inside the script. The atomic RMW still prevents double-SPENDING one key, so this is NOT a double-admit bug. The damage: the shared TAT is advanced with inconsistent time origins across nodes, so the enforced effective rate DRIFTS from contract and verdicts become node-dependent (same request allowed on a node whose clock is ahead, denied on one behind, with mismatched retry_after). An NTP step BACKWARD writes TAT far in the future -> that tenant is mass-false-denied (locked out) until real time catches up; a step FORWARD -> a one-shot boundary burst of false-allows. Subtlety: atomicity does NOT imply a consistent clock, and the 'replication-safe' refactor is exactly what breaks it. Fix: redis.call('TIME') as sole clock + redis.replicate_commands() (effects replication) — replication safety AND one clock.

PITFALL 2 — TTL/maxmemory eviction silently resetting the GCRA key, correlated with load. (a) TTL refreshed only on ALLOW -> a tenant pinned at its limit is being DENIED every request, its TTL never extended, key expires mid-throttle, next request finds no key -> tat=now -> full fresh burst every TTL. (b) Under memory pressure allkeys-lru/random evicts limiter keys REGARDLESS of TTL, and memory pressure correlates with high traffic, so the busiest tenants' counters silently reset exactly when most loaded, with no error trail. Note volatile-ttl is NOT a safeguard: limiter keys carry a TTL so volatile-ttl evicts precisely them. Fix: PEXPIRE >= tau+T on EVERY access including denies; store state in a logical DB/instance with noeviction; treat limiter-key eviction as a correctness incident; set TTL >= time-to-decay-to-idle so eviction is a no-op.

PITFALL 3 — Token leasing over-admits up to lease_size x N, and the async refund path races into double-credit / negative counters — hitting exactly the low-rate tenant fairness protects. (a) Over-admission: N=50 nodes each holding a 10-token lease vs a 10-req/s contract -> up to 500 outstanding -> 50x over-admit, stolen from the pool. (b) Refund race: a lease-expiry timer refunds AND a failed-request handler refunds the same token, or a delayed refund lands after the aggregator reclaimed the expired lease -> counter credited above cap (over-admit) or driven negative (naive if tokens>0 reads 'empty forever' = false starvation). Interleave: lease id=7 (K=100) at t0, spends 60; at t0+100ms lease expires, node sends refund(7,40), packet delayed; aggregator at t0+100ms reclaims the 40; delayed refund(7,40) lands at t0+150ms and adds 40 AGAIN -> +40 phantom over C, drawn from another tenant's share. Subtlety: the ADMIT script's atomicity is necessary but NOT sufficient because refunds mutate the SAME state on a DIFFERENT async path. Fix: lease high-volume tenants only (a 10-req/s tenant gains nothing and is the one catastrophically over-admitted); bound lease by b_i and cap outstanding via rl:lease:{tid}:* (Sum(leases)<=b_i); reclaim leaked leases by per-lease TTL not by trusting a node; make refunds idempotent by leaseId (SET refunded:{id} NX); route every mutation through the same atomic Lua.

(Honorable mention 4th trap: assuming the floor+pool Lua script is atomic in Redis Cluster — it is not across slots (§3). Testing on a single instance then deploying to a cluster yields CROSSSLOT errors or a silently-approximate cap.)

## 6. Cross-regime check
No starvation: private floor key (normal) -> per-node r_i/N_est GCRA biased high (outage) -> forgive-not-back-charge reseed TAT=max(stored,now) (recovery). Caveat: outage floor preservation is exact only under even spread.
No herd: continuous GCRA (no shared zero-crossing) + jittered retry_after (normal) -> frozen pool + continuous local buckets (outage) -> staggered reconnect + no-free-burst seed + clamped refill (recovery).
Neither property is traded for the other in any regime — EXCEPT that exact global-capacity fairness among borrowers is deliberately relaxed to 'approximate' in a clustered deployment, because Redis Lua atomicity does not span shards. That is the one place the design chooses honesty over an unattainable clean invariant.

A simple counterexample refutes 'correct': with a per-tenant borrow cap, if only one tenant is active it can be denied despite idle global capacity, so the scheme is not generally fair/work-conserving and thus not universally correct.

Below is the complete deliverable. It is written as a normative specification (English, technical), self-contained, and decisive: every choice is stated, ISO ambiguities are resolved explicitly, and the final section proves totality.

---

# Specification: `parse_iso8601_duration(s)`

## 0. Scope, signature, and result domain

`parse_iso8601_duration(s)` maps an arbitrary input value to exactly one of two tagged outcomes:

```
Result = Ok(NormalizedDuration) | Err(ParseError)
```

- The function never returns `None`, never returns an untagged value, never mutates `s`, never performs I/O, never raises an *undeclared* exception. (Whether `Err` is delivered as a raised exception or a returned value is an implementation binding; the *outcome set* is what this spec fixes. I write it as a returned tagged union.)
- It is **deterministic**, **idempotent** (parsing the same string twice yields equal results), and **pure**.

```
NormalizedDuration {
  profile:  "default",         // see §7 for extended profiles
  sign:     +1,                // -1 only reachable in the extended signed profile
  years:    Rational >= 0,     // exact, arbitrary precision
  months:   Rational >= 0,
  weeks:    Rational >= 0,     // nonzero only in the week form
  days:     Rational >= 0,
  hours:    Rational >= 0,
  minutes:  Rational >= 0,
  seconds:  Rational >= 0,
  present:  Set<Component>,     // which designators actually appeared
  had_T:    bool               // whether the 'T' designator was present
}
ParseError { code: ErrorCode, position: int /* 0-based code-point index, or -1 */, message: str }
```

**Numeric model.** All magnitudes are held as *exact rationals* (integer numerator/denominator), never binary floats. `PT0.1S` yields `seconds = 1/10` exactly. No unit conversion is performed between calendar-variable units (years/months/days are NOT summed or reduced), because their lengths are context-dependent; the parser is a *syntactic-to-structured* map, not a time arithmetic engine. Absent components are exact `0`. `present` and `had_T` are retained so that representationally distinct zeros (`P0D` vs `PT0S`) remain distinguishable; numeric-value equality that ignores this is an optional coarser equivalence (§6.2).

---

## 1. Lexical alphabet (what characters even mean)

Input is a finite sequence of Unicode code points. Only the following ASCII code points are *meaningful*; every other code point is a lexical error at its position (§5, `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR` and its named refinements).

| Class | Exact code points |
|---|---|
| DIGIT | `U+0030`–`U+0039` (`0`–`9`) **only** |
| Date designators | `P Y M W D` (`U+0050 U+0059 U+004D U+0057 U+0044`) |
| Time designator / time units | `T H M S` (`U+0054 U+0048 U+004D U+0053`) |
| Decimal separator | `.` (`U+002E`) or `,` (`U+002C`) — both accepted, ISO permits either |
| Sign (extended profile only) | `+` (`U+002B`) or `-` (`U+002D`) |

Explicit **non-members** (all rejected): every non-ASCII digit (Arabic-Indic `٠-٩ U+0660-0669`, Extended Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, fullwidth `０-９ U+FF10-FF19`, superscripts, `U+2460`-style enclosed digits, etc.), all lowercase letters, all whitespace (`U+0020`, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, NBSP `U+00A0`, `U+FEFF` BOM), all control characters (incl. `U+0000`), Roman-numeral/letterlike look-alikes, and any punctuation not listed above. There is **no** Unicode NFC/NFKC normalization and **no** case folding: `٣`, `１`, `p`, `y` are *not* silently mapped to `3`, `1`, `P`, `Y`.

---

## 2. Grammar (ABNF) — the context-free skeleton

```abnf
duration        = [ sign ] "P" body
sign            = "+" / "-"                  ; DEFAULT PROFILE: rejected (E_SIGNED_VALUE)
body            = week-form / date-time-form

week-form       = weeks
date-time-form  = date-part [ "T" time-part ]

date-part       = [ years ] [ months ] [ days ]
time-part       = [ hours ] [ minutes ] [ seconds ]

years   = number "Y"
months  = number "M"        ; 'M' BEFORE 'T'  = months
weeks   = number "W"
days    = number "D"
hours   = number "H"
minutes = number "M"        ; 'M' AFTER  'T'  = minutes
seconds = number "S"

number  = int [ frac ]
int     = 1*DIGIT           ; integer part MANDATORY; leading zeros allowed
frac    = ("." / ",") 1*DIGIT   ; at least one fractional digit
DIGIT   = %x30-39
```

The ABNF alone is insufficient (it permits `P`, `PT`, out-of-order and duplicate tokens, weeks mixed with others, fractions on every token, and the `M` ambiguity). Those are pinned by the context-sensitive constraints in §3, which are **normative and override** any latitude the ABNF appears to grant.

---

## 3. Context-sensitive constraints (the real rules)

- **C1 — Non-empty.** At least one of the seven components must be present. `P` and `PT` are invalid.
- **C2 — T iff time.** The literal `T` is present **iff** at least one time component (`H`, minutes-`M`, or `S`) is present. A `T` with no following time component is invalid (`E_DANGLING_T`). A time-only unit reachable without a preceding `T` (i.e. `H` or `S` occurring while still in the date section) is invalid (`E_TIME_WITHOUT_T`). (`M` alone cannot force this, because a pre-`T` `M` is *defined* to be months; see C7.)
- **C3 — Canonical order.** Within the date part the order is `Y, M, W, D`; within the time part `H, M, S`. Any token that appears after a token of equal-or-lower rank has already appeared, or out of these sequences, is `E_ORDER`. (Because `W` is exclusive (C5), the practical date order is `Y, M, D`.)
- **C4 — No duplicates.** Each of the seven *components* appears at most once. Note this is by component, not by letter: `P1MT1M` (months + minutes) is **valid** — two `M` letters, two *different* components.
- **C5 — Week exclusivity.** The week form is mutually exclusive with every other component. Any `W` combined with any of `Y/M/D/H/M/S` (in either order) is `E_WEEK_MIXED`.
- **C6 — Fraction placement.** At most one `frac` may occur in the whole string, and it must be on the **last component token present** (equivalently, the lowest-order present component). Given C3, "lowest-order present" ≡ "the final token," so the rule reduces to: *a fraction is legal only on the final component.* Any fraction on a non-final token, or a second fraction, is `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT`. This is the standards-faithful ISO 8601 rule (fraction on the smallest value), generalized beyond seconds (see §7 for the seconds-only strict profile). Consequence: `P0.5Y`, `PT2.5H`, `P1.5W` are valid; `P1.5YT1H`, `PT2.5H30S` are not.
- **C7 — `M` disambiguation.** An `M` encountered while the scanner is in the date section denotes months; an `M` encountered after the `T` transition denotes minutes. This is fully determined by position; no lookahead heuristic is used.
- **C8 — Number well-formedness.** Every component needs a mandatory integer part (`≥1` digit) and, if a separator appears, `≥1` fractional digit. `P.5Y`, `PT5.S`, `PT5..5S`, `PT5.,5S` are malformed (`E_NUMBER_FORMAT`). A designator with no number (`PY`, `PT S`) is `E_MISSING_NUMBER`.
- **C9 — No stray input.** After the final `S`/`W`/etc., no further code points may remain; any residue is `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR` (a.k.a. trailing garbage). No leading, trailing, or interior whitespace is tolerated.

---

## 4. Normalization (what a valid parse produces)

For a valid string, each present component's rational value is placed in its field; absent fields are `0`; `present` records the appearing components; `had_T` records `T` presence; `sign = +1` (default profile). No cross-unit reduction is performed. Weeks are retained in `weeks` (they are exactly 7 days, so a `weeks → days ×7` canonicalization is *lossless* and offered as an optional variant, but the default keeps `weeks` distinct to preserve the week form's identity). Examples:

- `P3Y6M4DT12H30M5S` → `{y3, mo6, d4, h12, min30, s5, present={Y,Mo,D,H,Min,S}, had_T=true}`
- `PT0S` → `{all 0 except s=0 present}, present={S}, had_T=true}`
- `P1W` → `{weeks=1, present={W}, had_T=false}`
- `PT0.5S` / `PT0,5S` → `{seconds = 1/2}`
- `P1MT1M` → `{months=1, minutes=1}`

---

## 5. Error taxonomy (defined outcomes)

Codes are listed with their **priority rank** (used only for same-position tie-breaks, §5.1). Every `Err` carries the 0-based code-point `position` of the offending point (`-1` for whole-input conditions: type, empty).

| Rank | Code | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `E_TYPE` | `s` is not a `str` (e.g. `None`, `int`, `bytes`, list). `position = -1`. |
| 2 | `E_EMPTY` | `s == ""`. `position = -1`. |
| 3 | `E_SIGNED_VALUE` | A leading `+`/`-` (default profile), or any per-component sign such as `P-1Y` (always). |
| 4 | `E_NO_P` | After the optional sign slot, the next code point is not `P` (includes lowercase `p`, leading whitespace, `3Y`, `1W`). |
| 5 | `E_LOWERCASE_DESIGNATOR` | A code point that is the ASCII lowercase of a valid designator appears where a designator is expected (`P1y`, `P1yT`). Diagnostic refinement of `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR`. |
| 6 | `E_NON_ASCII_DIGIT` | A non-ASCII digit appears where a digit could go (`P٣Y`, `P１Y`). Refinement of `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR`. |
| 7 | `E_MISSING_NUMBER` | A designator appears where a number was required (`PY`, `PTM`). |
| 8 | `E_NUMBER_FORMAT` | Malformed number: no integer digit before separator (`P.5Y`), no digit after separator (`PT5.S`), double/adjacent separators (`PT5..5S`, `PT5.,5S`). |
| 9 | `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` | A fraction on a non-final component, or a second fraction (`P1.5YT1H`, `PT2.5H30S`). |
| 10 | `E_ORDER` | Component out of canonical order, or a date-only unit after `T` / duplicated-rank violation (`P1M1Y`, `PT1Y`, `P1D1M`). |
| 11 | `E_DUPLICATE` | Same *component* twice (`P1Y1Y`, `PT1H1H`). |
| 12 | `E_WEEK_MIXED` | Week combined with any other component (`P1W1D`, `P1D1W`, `P1WT1H`). |
| 13 | `E_TIME_WITHOUT_T` | A time-only unit (`H` or `S`) reached with no preceding `T` (`P1H`, `P5S`). |
| 14 | `E_DANGLING_T` | `T` present with no following time component (`PT`, `P1YT`, `P1DT`). |
| 15 | `E_EMPTY_DURATION` | `P` (or extended `-P`) with zero components total (`P`). Distinct from `E_DANGLING_T`. |
| 16 | `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR` | Any other unexpected/stray code point, including trailing garbage and interior whitespace (`P1Y `, `P1Y#`, `P1 Y`). |
| 17 | `E_MISSING_DESIGNATOR` | A number consumed but end-of-input reached before its designator (`P5`, `PT5`). |
| 18 | `E_OVERFLOW` | *Bounded profile only* (§7): a magnitude exceeds the profile's declared numeric range. Never raised in the default arbitrary-precision profile. |

### 5.1 Uniqueness of the reported error (single-outcome guarantee)

When multiple constraints are violated, the reported error is selected deterministically:

1. **Earliest position wins.** The scanner runs strictly left-to-right and reports the violation at the smallest code-point index.
2. **Rank breaks ties.** If two conditions genuinely apply at the *same* index, the lower rank number in §5 wins.

This makes the error-valued outcome a *function* (single-valued) of the input, which is essential for totality. Examples of the rule at work: `PT0.5S0.5S` → the duplicate `S` at its position outranks nothing earlier, and the second fraction is at a later index than the duplicate token boundary → `E_DUPLICATE` (earliest structural violation). `1W` → `E_NO_P` at index 0 (fires before any week-mixing analysis). `-p1y` (default) → sign at index 0 → `E_SIGNED_VALUE` (rank 3) before the lowercase check.

---

## 6. Comprehensive edge-case enumeration

Every requested adversarial class, plus the exhaustive partition, with the exact outcome.

### 6.1 Accept-with-value

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `P3Y6M4DT12H30M5S` | Ok — all six fields set |
| `PT0S` | Ok — `seconds=0`, `had_T=true` (valid: one time component present) |
| `P0D` | Ok — `days=0` (valid zero duration; distinct from `PT0S` via `present`/`had_T`) |
| `P1W` | Ok — `weeks=1` |
| `P0W` | Ok — `weeks=0` |
| `P1.5W`, `P1,5W` | Ok — `weeks=3/2` (fraction on only/final component) |
| `P0.5Y` | Ok — `years=1/2` (fraction on lowest present) |
| `PT2.5H` | Ok — `hours=5/2` |
| `PT0.1S`, `PT0,1S` | Ok — `seconds=1/10` (exact rational) |
| `P1M` | Ok — `months=1` (pre-`T` `M`) |
| `PT1M` | Ok — `minutes=1` (post-`T` `M`) |
| `P1MT1M` | Ok — `months=1, minutes=1` (two `M`, different components; not a duplicate) |
| `P1DT1H`, `PT36H`, `P007Y` | Ok — no range cap on hours; leading zeros allowed → `years=7` |
| `P999999999999999999999Y` | **Ok** in default profile (arbitrary precision); `E_OVERFLOW` only under a bounded profile |

### 6.2 Empty / structural-emptiness

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `""` | `E_EMPTY` |
| `P` | `E_EMPTY_DURATION` |
| `PT` | `E_DANGLING_T` (T present, zero time components) |
| `P1YT`, `P1DT`, `P1MT` | `E_DANGLING_T` |

Note `P0D` and `PT0S` are both valid and, at the numeric level, all-zero. The default equality retains `present`/`had_T`, so they are **distinct** `NormalizedDuration` values. An optional coarser "magnitude equivalence" that compares only the seven rationals treats them as equal; both relations are defined, and the spec exposes both.

### 6.3 Missing `P`

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `3Y`, `1W`, `T1H` | `E_NO_P` at index 0 |
| ` P1Y` (leading space) | `E_NO_P` at index 0 (no leading whitespace permitted) |

### 6.4 `T` with no time parts / time without `T`

Covered above: `PT`, `P1YT` → `E_DANGLING_T`. Conversely `P1H`, `P5S` → `E_TIME_WITHOUT_T` (a time-only unit surfaced before any `T`). `P1YT` vs `P1H` are deliberately different codes because the failures are different (dangling designator vs misplaced unit).

### 6.5 Out-of-order components

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `P1M1Y` (M then Y) | `E_ORDER` at the `Y` |
| `P1D1M` (D then months-M) | `E_ORDER` |
| `PT1Y` (date unit after T) | `E_ORDER` (Y is date-only; illegal in time part) |
| `PT30M1H` (min then hour) | `E_ORDER` |
| `PT1S30M` | `E_ORDER` |

### 6.6 Fractional seconds vs fractional other fields

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `PT1.5S`, `PT0,5S` | Ok (fraction on final) |
| `P0.5Y`, `PT2.5H`, `P1.25D`, `P1.5W` | Ok when that component is the final present one |
| `P1.5YT1H` | `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` (years not final) |
| `PT2.5H30S` | `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` (hours not final) |
| `PT1.5M0S` | `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` (minutes not final) |
| `PT1.5M` | Ok (minutes final) |
| `P1.5DT0.5H` | `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` (two fractions; first is non-final) |

Under the **strict seconds-only profile** (§7), every fractional non-seconds field instead yields `E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT` even when final (e.g. `P0.5Y` → error); only `S` may carry a fraction.

### 6.7 Negative / signed values

| Input | Default outcome | Extended-signed profile |
|---|---|---|
| `-P1Y` | `E_SIGNED_VALUE` | Ok, `sign=-1` |
| `+P1Y` | `E_SIGNED_VALUE` | Ok, `sign=+1` |
| `P-1Y` (per-component) | `E_SIGNED_VALUE` | `E_SIGNED_VALUE` (per-component signs never allowed) |

Fractions with enormous denominators (`PT0.<10^6 digits>S`) are likewise accepted exactly in the default profile. There is no floating-point rounding, hence no silent overflow-to-infinity.

## 7. Profiles (all optional, default is fixed)

The **default profile** is the one specified above: uppercase-only, unsigned, ASCII-digits-only, fraction on final component, arbitrary precision, both `.`/`,` accepted. Named opt-in profiles, each of which only *relaxes or tightens* defined behavior (never introduces undefined behavior):

- **signed**: permit one leading `+`/`-`, setting `sign`. Per-component signs still rejected.
- **case-insensitive**: fold ASCII case of designators before validation.
- **seconds-only-fraction**: fractions permitted only on `S` (matches `java.time`, XML-Schema-like strictness).
- **bounded(range)**: enforce a numeric range and emit `E_OVERFLOW` beyond it.
- **comma-only / period-only**: restrict the decimal separator.

A profile is a parameter of the function; with no profile argument, the default applies. Each profile still yields the total `Ok | Err` contract.

## 8. Reference algorithm (constructive witness of totality)

```
parse(s, profile=default):
  if not isinstance(s, str): return Err(E_TYPE, -1)          # (A) type guard
  if len(s) == 0:            return Err(E_EMPTY, -1)          # (B) empty guard
  i = 0                                                       # code-point cursor
  # --- sign slot ---
  if s[0] in {'+','-'}:
      if not profile.signed: return Err(E_SIGNED_VALUE, 0)
      sign = -1 if s[0]=='-' else +1; i = 1
  else: sign = +1
  # --- mandatory P ---
  if i >= len(s) or s[i] != (fold(s[i]) if profile.ci else s[i])=='P' ... :
      if i >= len(s) or s[i] != 'P': return Err(E_NO_P, i)
  i += 1
  state = DATE            # DATE -> (T seen) -> TIME
  last_rank = -inf        # for order/duplicate enforcement
  present = {}; had_T = False; frac_seen_on_nonfinal = False
  fields = zeros()
  while i < len(s):                                           # (C) each iteration advances i by >=1
      c = s[i]
      if c == 'T':
          if state == TIME or had_T: return Err(E_ORDER, i)   # stray/second T
          had_T = True; state = TIME; last_rank = -inf; i += 1; continue
      if is_ascii_digit(c) or c in {'.',','}:
          (value, had_frac, j, numerr) = read_number(s, i, profile)
          if numerr: return Err(numerr.code, numerr.pos)      # E_NUMBER_FORMAT
          if j >= len(s): return Err(E_MISSING_DESIGNATOR, i)
          d = s[j]
          comp = classify_designator(d, state)                # uses C7 for 'M'
          if comp is LOWERCASE:      return Err(E_LOWERCASE_DESIGNATOR, j)
          if comp is INVALID:        return Err(E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR, j)
          if comp is TIME_UNIT and not had_T:
                                     return Err(E_TIME_WITHOUT_T, j)
          if comp is WEEK and present nonempty, or present has WEEK:
                                     return Err(E_WEEK_MIXED, j)
          if comp in present:        return Err(E_DUPLICATE, j)
          if rank(comp) <= last_rank:return Err(E_ORDER, j)
          if had_frac: record_frac_position(comp, j)          # validate against "final" at EOF
          if profile.seconds_only_fraction and had_frac and comp != SECONDS:
                                     return Err(E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT, j)
          fields[comp] = value; present.add(comp); last_rank = rank(comp); i = j+1; continue
      if is_non_ascii_digit(c):      return Err(E_NON_ASCII_DIGIT, i)
      if is_lowercase_designator(c): return Err(E_LOWERCASE_DESIGNATOR, i)
      if is_designator(c):           return Err(E_MISSING_NUMBER, i)   # designator w/o number
      return Err(E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR, i)
  # --- end-of-input constraints ---
  if had_T and no time component in present: return Err(E_DANGLING_T, pos_of_T)
  if present is empty:                        return Err(E_EMPTY_DURATION, i_after_P)
  if a recorded fraction is not on the final present token:
                                              return Err(E_FRACTION_PLACEMENT, that_pos)  # C6
  if profile.bounded and any field out of range:
                                              return Err(E_OVERFLOW, offending_pos)
  return Ok(NormalizedDuration{sign, fields..., present, had_T, profile})
```

`read_number` consumes `1*DIGIT [ (.|,) 1*DIGIT ]`, returning `E_NUMBER_FORMAT` for a missing integer part (separator-first), a missing fractional digit, or adjacent separators; it never loops without advancing.

## 9. Totality argument

**Claim.** For every possible input value `x`, `parse(x)` returns exactly one `Ok(...)` or one `Err(...)`, and always terminates.

1. **Domain coverage.** The first statement (A) handles every value that is not a `str` via `E_TYPE`. Below it, `x` is a `str` — a finite sequence of code points — so all remaining reasoning is over finite sequences.
2. **Termination.** The only loop is the scan `while i < len(s)`. Every branch inside it either `return`s or advances `i` by at least one (the `T` branch `i+=1`; the number branch sets `i = j+1` with `j ≥ i`; every error branch returns). Therefore `i` strictly increases until it reaches `len(s)`; the loop executes at most `len(s)` times and halts. `read_number` similarly advances its cursor monotonically over a finite string. Hence no infinite loops and no unbounded recursion (there is none).
3. **No fall-through.** The scan body is a total case analysis on the current code point `c`: it is `T`, or a digit/separator (number path), or a non-ASCII digit, or a lowercase designator, or an uppercase designator without a number, or *anything else* (`E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR`). These cases are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive over all code points, so every character maps to a defined action. The number path itself is total: `read_number` returns either a value or a defined `E_NUMBER_FORMAT`, and the following designator is classified into `{valid-component, lowercase, invalid, missing}` — again exhaustive.
4. **Post-loop is total.** After the loop, a fixed sequence of guarded returns covers dangling `T`, empty duration, fraction placement, and (profile) overflow; if none fire, it returns `Ok`. There is no path that reaches the end of the function without returning.
5. **Single-valuedness.** By §5.1 the first `return Err` encountered is at the earliest offending index, and same-index ties are broken by the fixed rank order. Because the scan visits indices in strictly increasing order and each index yields at most one classification, the earliest error is unique; thus the error outcome is a *function* of the input, not a relation. Valid inputs likewise map to a unique `NormalizedDuration` because field assignment is deterministic and order/duplicate constraints forbid ambiguous re-assignment.
6. **Every enumerated adversarial class lands.** §6's table is a partition of the interesting input space, and each row names the specific defined outcome; the reference algorithm's structure shows the corresponding branch. Inputs not in any "interesting" row (e.g. arbitrary junk `"@@@"`, `"P␀"`, a lone emoji) fall to `E_UNEXPECTED_CHAR` or, before `P`, to `E_NO_P` — both defined.

Therefore the mapping `input ↦ outcome` is **total** (defined on all inputs), **single-valued** (deterministic), and **terminating** — i.e. `parse_iso8601_duration` is a total function. ∎

## 10. Summary of the load-bearing decisions (so reviewers can override deliberately)

1. ASCII digits only; Unicode digits are hard-rejected (`E_NON_ASCII_DIGIT`), no NFKC folding.
2. Uppercase-only designators; lowercase rejected by default (case-insensitive is an opt-in profile).
3. Unsigned by default; signs are an opt-in profile; per-component signs never allowed.
4. Fraction on the **lowest-order present** component (ISO-faithful), tightenable to seconds-only.
5. Both `.` and `,` accepted as decimal separators.
6. Exact-rational, arbitrary-precision numerics; overflow only exists in an explicit bounded profile.
7. No cross-unit calendar arithmetic; weeks kept distinct; `present`/`had_T` retained so `P0D` ≠ `PT0S` structurally.
8. Errors report the earliest offending position; same-position ties broken by a fixed code rank, guaranteeing a unique outcome.

# Specification: `parse_iso8601_duration(s)`

**Version 1.0 — normative unless marked *(informative)*.**
Profile: strict ISO 8601-1:2019 §5.5.2 duration (designator format), with every profile decision the standard leaves open fixed explicitly below. This spec is **total**: §11 proves every possible input maps to exactly one defined outcome.

---

## 1. Scope and non-goals

`parse_iso8601_duration(s)` maps an input value `s` to either a **`Duration` record** or exactly one **defined error**. It is a pure function: no I/O, no locale, no clock, no randomness; identical input always yields the identical outcome.

**Out of scope (all rejected by the grammar, each hitting a *defined* error — see §8):**

- ISO 8601-2 signed/negative durations (`-P1D`, `+P1D`) — rejected, `ERR_SIGN`.
- The alternative representation `P0003-06-04T12:30:05` (ISO 8601-1 §5.5.2.4) — rejected (`ERR_SIGN` at the first `-`; message explains).
- Intervals and repeats (`2026-01-01/P1Y`, `R5/P1D`) — rejected (`ERR_MISSING_P` or `ERR_UNEXPECTED_CHAR`).
- Unit conversion/normalization across units (months→days, `PT24H`→`P1D`, `P1W`→`P7D`): **never performed** (calendar-dependent; `P1M` and `P30D` are distinct values of this function).
- Conversion to total seconds, comparison, arithmetic.

---

## 2. Input domain

The ambient input universe is **all values** the host language can pass.

- **D1.** If `s` is not a Unicode string (sequence of Unicode code points) — e.g. `None`, `bytes`, `int`, `float`, list — outcome is `ERR_TYPE` (Python binding: raise `TypeError`). Byte strings are *not* decoded; decoding is the caller's contract.
- **D2.** Otherwise `s` is a finite sequence of code points `s[0..n-1]`, `n ≥ 0`. Lone surrogates, NUL, controls, any code point whatsoever are in-domain and handled by the character-class partition in §7.
- **D3.** **No Unicode normalization** (no NFC/NFKC, no case folding) is applied. Comparison is raw code-point equality. Consequences: fullwidth `Ｐ` (U+FF30), Cyrillic `Р` (U+0420), fullwidth digits `３` are *not* `P`/digits and are rejected.
- **D4.** Length cap: `MAX_LEN = 4096` code points. If `n > MAX_LEN`: `ERR_TOO_LONG`. (Bounds memory/CPU for adversarial inputs while permitting exact big-number semantics, §6.)

---

## 3. Result type

```
Duration := {
  years   : Q≥0,   months  : Q≥0,   weeks : Q≥0,   days : Q≥0,
  hours   : Q≥0,   minutes : Q≥0,   seconds : Q≥0,
  form    : "week" | "components"
}
```

`Q≥0` = **exact** non-negative rational whose denominator is a power of 10 (i.e., an exact decimal). Binding recommendation: `fractions.Fraction`, `decimal.Decimal` (exact), or `(int numerator, int pow10)`. **Binary floats are forbidden as the stored representation**: `parse("PT0.1S").seconds` must equal exactly 1/10.

**Invariants (guaranteed on every accepted parse):**

- **I1.** `form == "week"` ⟹ all fields except `weeks` are 0. `form == "components"` ⟹ `weeks == 0`.
- **I2.** At most one field has a non-integral *lexical source*, and if so it is the lowest-order (last) component present in the input (§5, F-rules).
- **I3.** All fields ≥ 0 (no signs exist in the grammar).
- **I4.** Absent components are exactly 0. Lexical details (leading zeros `P01D`, trailing fraction zeros `P1.0D`, `,` vs `.`) are **not** preserved; only the numeric value is. Field magnitudes are bounded by `MAX_LEN` (≤ 10^4094).
- **I5.** Two accepted parses are equal iff field-wise numerically equal and `form` equal.

Note: `"P0D"`, `"PT0S"`, `"P0W"` all accept and yield all-zero fields (differing only in `form` for the last). The zero duration is representable; bare `"P"` is not it (rejected, §5 C1).

---

## 4. Error model

Abstract outcome: `Ok(Duration) | Err(code, pos, message)`.

- `pos` = 0-based code-point index of the first offending position; `pos = n` (one past end) for end-of-input errors; `pos = None` for `ERR_TYPE`/`ERR_TOO_LONG`/`ERR_EMPTY`.
- Python binding: return `Duration` on success; raise `DurationParseError(code, pos, message)` (subclass of `ValueError`) for all errors except non-string input, which raises `TypeError`. Raising vs. returning `Err` is a binding detail; the *outcome set* is identical.
- **Determinism rule:** the outcome is defined by the single left-to-right pass of §7. The **first** failing position determines the error; there is no backtracking, so exactly one code applies to any input.

**Error codes (closed set, 15):**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ERR_TYPE` | input is not a Unicode string |
| `ERR_EMPTY` | empty string `""` |
| `ERR_TOO_LONG` | length > `MAX_LEN` |
| `ERR_MISSING_P` | first code point is not `P` (U+0050) and not a sign |
| `ERR_SIGN` | `+` (U+002B), `-` (U+002D), or `−` (U+2212) encountered anywhere |
| `ERR_UNEXPECTED_CHAR` | code point not valid at this position (whitespace, lowercase at start of a component, Unicode digits, `/`, NUL, homoglyphs, …) |
| `ERR_MISSING_DIGITS` | designator with no preceding number (`PD`, `P1DD`) |
| `ERR_MISSING_DESIGNATOR` | number not followed by a valid designator (`P1`, `PT5`, `PT1e5S`, `P1y`) |
| `ERR_MISPLACED_DESIGNATOR` | time designator before `T` (`P1H`, `P1S`) or date/week designator after `T` (`PT1D`, `PT1Y`, `PT1W`) |
| `ERR_ORDER` | designator repeated or out of order within its section (`P1M1Y`, `PT1S1M`, `P1Y2Y`) |
| `ERR_WEEK_MIXED` | `W` combined with any other component (`P1W2D`, `P1Y1W`, `P1WT1H`, `P1W1W`) |
| `ERR_TIME_EMPTY` | `T` present but no time component follows (`PT`, `P1DT`) |
| `ERR_EMPTY_SPEC` | `P` with zero components (`"P"`) |
| `ERR_FRACTION_MALFORMED` | separator without digits on both sides (`PT.5S`, `PT5.S`, `PT1.2.3S`, `PT1.,5S`) |
| `ERR_FRACTION_NOT_LAST` | a fractional number is followed by any further component or `T` (`P0.5Y1M`, `PT1.5H30M`, `P0.5YT1H`) |

## 5. Accepted grammar (normative)

Terminals are exact code points: `P`=U+0050, `T`=U+0054, `Y M D W H S` = U+0059/4D/44/57/48/53, digits = U+0030–U+0039 **only**, decimal marks `.`=U+002E and `,`=U+002C (both accepted, per ISO which prefers comma but permits dot).

ABNF (RFC 5234), fully expanded so that "at least one component" is structural:

```abnf
duration   = %x50 ( week-form / general-form )        ; "P"

week-form  = number %x57                              ; nW  — nothing before or after

general-form = date-part [ time-part ]                ; but not both absent:
             ;   general-form = date-part time-part
             ;                / date-part
             ;                / time-part
date-part  = y-comp [mo-comp] [d-comp]
           / mo-comp [d-comp]
           / d-comp
time-part  = %x54 t-comps                             ; "T"
t-comps    = h-comp [mi-comp] [s-comp]
           / mi-comp [s-comp]
           / s-comp

y-comp  = number %x59        mo-comp = number %x4D
d-comp  = number %x44        h-comp  = number %x48
mi-comp = number %x4D        s-comp  = number %x53
number  = 1*DIGIT [ dec-mark 1*DIGIT ]
dec-mark = %x2E / %x2C
DIGIT   = %x30-39
```

**Side conditions (context-sensitive, normative):**

- **C1 (non-empty):** at least one component overall — structurally enforced above; bare `P` and bare `PT` are underivable.
- **C2 (T iff time):** `T` appears **iff** ≥1 time component is present, and time components appear **only** after `T`. Structurally enforced: `t-comps` is non-empty; `H`/`S` don't occur in `date-part`; the `M` before `T` is months, after `T` is minutes (the grammar disambiguates the overloaded `M` purely by position relative to `T`).
- **C3 (order, no repeats):** within each section components appear at most once, in the fixed order `Y M D` / `H M S` — structurally enforced above.
- **C4 (anchored):** the entire string must be a `duration`; no leading/trailing/internal extra code points of any kind (including all Unicode whitespace, BOM, ZWSP).
- **F1 (fraction placement):** a `number` may carry a fraction **only if** its component is the *last* component of the whole duration (the lowest-order component present). This applies uniformly, including `week-form` (`P0.5W` valid) and date-only forms (`P1.5D` valid; `P1.5DT1H` invalid). This is ISO 8601-1's "fraction only in the lowest-order component", chosen here over the stricter "seconds only" profile — the choice is fixed, not configurable.
- **F2 (fraction shape):** ≥1 digit before and ≥1 digit after the mark; exactly one mark per number.

**Explicitly outside the grammar (hence rejected):** signs anywhere; lowercase or non-ASCII designators; non-ASCII digits; exponents (`1e5`); underscores/group separators; whitespace; `W` mixed with anything; multiple `T`; components after a fractional component.

*(Informative)* Equivalent anchored regex — **must** be compiled with ASCII-only `\d` (Python: `re.ASCII`), and needs three post-checks (≥1 group matched; if `T` matched then ≥1 of H/M/S matched; fraction only in last matched group). The DFA of §7 is normative; the regex loses error positions/codes:

```
^P(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)W
   |(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)Y)?(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)M)?(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)D)?
    (?:T(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)H)?(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)M)?(?:(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)S)?)?)$
```

## 6. Semantic mapping (lexical → value)

For each matched `number` with integer digit string `a` and optional fraction digit string `b`:

```
value = int10(a) + int10(b) / 10^len(b)        (exactly; b absent ⇒ value = int10(a))
```

`int10` interprets **ASCII digits only**, arbitrary precision (bignum). Leading zeros are legal and insignificant (`P007Y` ⇒ years = 7). No rounding ever occurs; `MAX_LEN` bounds all magnitudes, so no overflow error exists or is needed. `form` = `"week"` for `week-form`, else `"components"`. Unmatched fields = 0.

*(Informative, adversarial implementation notes)* Do **not** implement `int10` with the host's general parsers: Python `int("١٢٣")` = 123 (Unicode digits), `int(" 12\n")` = 12 (whitespace), `int("1_0")` = 10 (underscores), `float("1e5")`/`float("inf")` accept exponents/infinities. The DFA below only ever accumulates code points U+0030–U+0039, which makes those hazards unreachable.

## 7. Normative parse algorithm (single-pass DFA)

Character classes partition **all** of Unicode: `{P} {T} {Y} {M} {D} {W} {H} {S} {0-9 ASCII} {. ,} {+ - −(U+2212)} {everything else}`. Every step consumes ≥1 code point or terminates; every class has a defined transition in every state (mostly → error), giving totality (§11).

```
1. not a Unicode string           → ERR_TYPE
2. n = 0                          → ERR_EMPTY
3. n > MAX_LEN                    → ERR_TOO_LONG
4. s[0] ∈ {+,-,−}                 → ERR_SIGN(0)
   s[0] ≠ 'P'                     → ERR_MISSING_P(0)     # incl. lowercase 'p': case-sensitive
5. i=1; section=DATE; last_rank=0; count=0; count_at_T=⊥; frac_seen=false; week=false; fields=0
   ranks: Y=1, M(date)=2, D=3 | H=5, M(time)=6, S=7
6. while i < n:
     c = s[i]
     c == 'T':
        section==TIME             → ERR_UNEXPECTED_CHAR(i)      # second T
        frac_seen                 → ERR_FRACTION_NOT_LAST(i)
        section=TIME; count_at_T=count; i++; continue
     c ∈ ASCII digits:
        frac_seen                 → ERR_FRACTION_NOT_LAST(i)
        scan a = 1*DIGIT (advance i)
        if s[i] ∈ {., ,}: j=i; i++; scan b = *DIGIT
             b empty              → ERR_FRACTION_MALFORMED(j)
             frac=true
        else frac=false
        i == n                    → ERR_MISSING_DESIGNATOR(n)   # e.g. "P1", "PT1.5"
        d = s[i]
        d ∈ {., ,}                → ERR_FRACTION_MALFORMED(i)   # "PT1.2.3S"
        d ∈ {+,-,−}               → ERR_SIGN(i)
        d == 'W':
             section==TIME        → ERR_MISPLACED_DESIGNATOR(i) # "PT1W"
             count > 0            → ERR_WEEK_MIXED(i)           # "P1Y1W"
             weeks=value(a,b); week=true; i++
             i == n               → ACCEPT (week form)
             s[i] ∈ digits∪{T,Y,M,D,W,H,S} → ERR_WEEK_MIXED(i)  # "P1W2D","P1WT1H","P1W1W"
             else                 → ERR_UNEXPECTED_CHAR(i)      # "P1Wx"
        d ∈ {H,S} ∧ section==DATE → ERR_MISPLACED_DESIGNATOR(i) # "P1H","P1S": T required
        d ∈ {Y,D} ∧ section==TIME → ERR_MISPLACED_DESIGNATOR(i) # "PT1Y","PT1D"
        d ∉ section's designators → ERR_MISSING_DESIGNATOR(i)   # "P1y","PT1e5S","P1_0D"
        rank(d,section) ≤ last_rank → ERR_ORDER(i)              # repeats & inversions
        field(d)=value(a,b); last_rank=rank; count++; frac_seen|=frac; i++; continue
     c ∈ {Y,M,D,W,H,S}            → ERR_MISSING_DIGITS(i)       # "PD", "P1DD"
     c ∈ {., ,}                   → ERR_FRACTION_MALFORMED(i)   # "PT.5S"
     c ∈ {+,-,−}                  → ERR_SIGN(i)                 # "P-1D", "P0003-06-04…"
     otherwise                    → ERR_UNEXPECTED_CHAR(i)      # whitespace, unicode digits, '/', NUL, lowercase mid-string start-of-component, …
7. end of input:
     week                         → ACCEPT                       # (already accepted inline)
     count_at_T ≠ ⊥ ∧ count == count_at_T → ERR_TIME_EMPTY(n)    # "PT", "P1DT"
     count == 0                   → ERR_EMPTY_SPEC(n)            # "P"
     ACCEPT → Duration(fields, form = "components")
```

The overloaded `M` is resolved by `section`: rank 2 (months) before `T`, rank 6 (minutes) after — so `P1MT1M` is legal (1 month, 1 minute).

Every class below has a defined outcome; classes jointly cover the whole input universe because they are the images of the DFA's states × character classes (§11).
